title: The multiplier process: one injection, shrinking rounds
subject: economics

scenes.caption: The circular flow: an injection enters
scenes.narration: Government spending injects $100 into firms. The money flows round the circular flow to households as income, ready to be spent again.

shape.explain: Government: its spending is an injection into the circular flow.
Label: the government, source of the injection.
Injection arrow: $100 of new spending enters firms from outside the flow.
Label: the injection is $100 of autonomous spending.
Households: they own the factors of production and receive income from firms.
Firms: they receive the injection and pay households for factors.
Label: households, one side of the circular flow.
Label: firms, the other side of the circular flow.
Spending flow: households spend their income with firms.
Income flow: firms pay households, carrying the injection round the flow.
Label: the top flow is spending from households to firms.
Label: the bottom flow carries goods, services and income back.
Spending token: the $100 injection, shown at firms on the flow path.

steps.text: A $100 government injection enters firms, then flows to households as income in the circular flow.

scenes.caption: Round 1: $100 in, $20 leaks out
scenes.narration: Households spend the $100 with firms in round 1. But $20 leaks out as saving, tax and imports, so the token shrinks: only $80 goes round again.

shape.explain: Households: they received $100 of income in round 1.
Firms: they receive the spending and pay out new income.
Label: households.
Label: firms.
Flow arrow: spending travels from households to firms.
Label: round 1 adds the full $100 injection to national income.
Spending token at full size: the whole $100 is spent in round 1.
Drain arrow: watch it grow downwards as $20 leaks out of the flow.
Leakages box: saving, tax and imports drain money out of the flow each round.
Label: $20 leaks out in round 1.
Label: the $20 that leaks away is not re-spent.
Bar baseline: the round income bars stand on this axis.
Round 1 bar: $100 of new income, the full injection.
Label: round 1 adds $100.
Label: the first round bar.
Running total marker: national income is up $100 after round 1.

steps.text: Round 1 adds $100 of income, but $20 leaks out, so only $80 is re-spent next round.

scenes.caption: Rounds 2 and 3 shrink: $80, then $64
scenes.narration: Each lap re-spends four-fifths of the last round. Round 2 adds $80 and round 3 adds $64, so the bars shrink geometrically while the total climbs to $244.

shape.explain: Households: they re-spend most of each round of income.
Firms: each round of spending becomes their income to pay out again.
Label: households.
Label: firms.
Label: rounds 2 and 3, each smaller than the last.
Spending token, already shrunk: $80 is re-spent in round 2.
Leakage arrow: a smaller leakage drains out of round 2.
Leakage arrow: a still smaller leakage drains out of round 3.
Label: leakages shrink as the rounds shrink.
Bar baseline: the round bars and the total bar stand on this axis.
Round 1 bar: $100, the full injection.
Round 2 bar: $80, four-fifths of round 1.
Round 3 bar: $64, four-fifths of round 2.
Label: round 1 adds $100.
Label: round 2 adds $80.
Label: round 3 adds $64.
Label: the round 1 bar.
Label: the round 2 bar.
Label: the round 3 bar.
Total bar: watch it grow as each round is added - it starts at the round 1 total.
Running total after round 2: $100 + $80 = $180.
Running total after round 3: $180 + $64 = $244.

steps.text: Rounds 2 and 3 add $80 then $64: each round is four-fifths of the last, and the running total climbs to $244.

scenes.caption: Aggregate demand settles at $500
scenes.narration: On the aggregate demand diagram the same story shows as shrinking shifts. AD moves right by less each round until national income settles at $500, five times the injection.

shape.explain: Total label: national income settles at $500, five times the $100 injection.
Price level axis: higher up means a higher price level.
National income axis: further right means more national income.
Label: the vertical axis measures the price level.
Label: the horizontal axis measures national income.
Aggregate supply curve: the price level rises as national income grows.
Label: AS is the aggregate supply curve.
AD1: aggregate demand before the injection works through.
AD on the move: watch it shift right in shrinking steps as the rounds are re-spent.
Label: AD1, the starting aggregate demand curve.
Label: the final aggregate demand curve after all the rounds.
Final equilibrium: aggregate demand finally crosses aggregate supply here, at $500 of national income.
Label: the final equilibrium, where AD final crosses AS.

steps.text: National income settles at $500: five times the $100 injection, so the multiplier is 5.
